title: The Moth in the Machine
description: One-minute skill: The Moth in the Machine.

hook.text: In 1947 a real moth got stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II. The first literal computer bug was born.

buildup.text: Grace Hopper's team taped the moth into the logbook with the note: 'First actual case of bug being found.'

discovery.text: The word 'bug' predates computers—Edison used it in 1878 for engineering flaws—but this made it famous.

twist.text: The moth didn't crash the system. The relay just ran slow. Most early bugs were subtle, not catastrophic.

climax.text: That logbook page is now in the Smithsonian. A dead moth became computing's most famous artifact.

punchline.text: The first bug was literally a bug.

quiz.question: Where was the first literal computer bug found?
